title: 1,700 Years of One Craft — China's Porcelain Capital | China Travel Expert
description:
For 1,700 years, one Chinese city has made porcelain — and almost nothing else. Why?

That city is Jingdezhen. Ceramics have been fired there for over 1,700 years, and it was named in the Song dynasty's Jingde reign (1004). From 1369, Ming emperors ran an Imperial Kiln Factory making porcelain for the court alone. The old saying describes the ware as "white as jade, thin as paper, sound like a chime, bright as a mirror" — and by the classic count in the Tiangong Kaiwu, a single piece passes through 72 pairs of hands before it is finished.

🧭 Expert Tip: Buy from a working kiln workshop, not the tourist stalls near the gate — you'll pay less and meet the person who made it.

一座城，只烧一件事，烧了1700年——白如玉，薄如纸。
